comment: T4 baseline (docs/TESTING.md). `nodes` counts every node and `retainedNodes` only those carrying a mesh of their own (the Labels). Since P1 all of them draw: `buffersAlive` is 2 whatever the node count - the growing vertex buffer and the fullscreen quad the filter passes draw - because no node owns one any more. It read 3 until the P1 review, and that 3 was a C function returning the literal 3: gated against the literal, so the assertion compared a constant to a constant and would have kept passing if every Label allocated a buffer again. It also miscounted, since the third thing it named was the font image and not a buffer. It is made-minus-freed at the sg_make_buffer/sg_destroy_buffer sites now, and was checked by allocating one extra buffer and watching it read 3, then 2 again, and `vertices` is what proves every label emitted geometry instead of being dropped by a full pool. `ui.draws` is 20000 and not 253 because the bench alternates a white-texture card with a font-texture label on every node; the unified pipeline and the white texel in the glyph atlas that collapse that are P2's. Counters gate hard; milliseconds only report, with a warn threshold, because this is a shared developer box. How much that matters, measured 2026-09-20 after the sampler commit: the same `benchSprites` binary that read 1.63 ms when this file was written reads 1.87-2.09 ms on a box sitting at 54% CPU from other work, which is 1.28x and most of the way to the 1.5x warn. The numbers below were not re-taken to make that go away, and the warn factor was not raised: a threshold moved to fit the reading stops being a threshold. What a millisecond row can answer is *relative* regression, and only one way - build both commits, run them interleaved on the same box in the same minute. Done for the sampler commit against its parent `06c2bd0`: PREV 1.96/2.09/1.87/2.00 against NOW 1.98/1.97/1.92/1.96, mean 1.98 vs 1.96, so guardrail 8 holds and the gap to 1.63 is the machine. A gate WARN on a millisecond row means re-run that A/B, not that the phase regressed — SCENE-SCALE.md:197 records its own numbers being taken at load average 14-17. buffersAlive 2 -> 3 on 2026-09-21, at P2's sprite pipeline: the third is the unit quad the instanced sprite path steps per vertex, a 48-byte static buffer made once at setup beside the growing vertex buffer and the filter passes' fullscreen quad. The gate caught this rather than a reader noticing - which is the point of the counter having been moved off a literal at P1, and it is the second time in one session it has earned that. What would make 3 wrong is growth with the node count: three is three at 10 000 nodes and at 20 000, and a number that scales is the defect this counter exists to catch. Keys are nested rather than dotted so tests/bench/check.ms can read them through the JsonValue accessors. MILLISECONDS RE-TAKEN 2026-09-21 (F-14, at P2's first step). The rows above used to read ui 17.8 and sprites 1.63, and neither could be reproduced by the very commit they came from. Measured on a QUIET box - 10.8% CPU mean over five one-second samples, checked before the runs and not after the fact - by an interleaved same-box A/B between 6a997ee (P1's land, rebuilt from a git archive) and 544ea4a, six alternating pairs of each bench: ui P1 19.95 (19.69-20.30) against NOW 19.86 (19.34-20.16); sprites P1 2.51 (2.24-3.06) against NOW 2.48 (2.27-2.82). A standalone eight-run series of the current binaries alone, which perturbs less, reads ui 20.33 (20.19-21.08) and sprites 2.76 (2.52-2.86). TWO CONCLUSIONS, both measured. (1) GUARDRAIL 8 HOLDS: nothing between P1's land and here - the commit hook, the rebase onto void3d's M6 - moved either row; the two columns of the A/B are inside each other's spread. (2) The old numbers were WRONG, not stale-because-busy. This file used to explain the gap to 1.63 as the machine, citing a run at 54% CPU. That explanation does not survive: at 10.8% CPU, P1's OWN binary reads 2.51. THIS IS NOT A THRESHOLD MOVED TO FIT A READING, which this file forbids and still forbids. warnFactor is unchanged at 1.5. What changed is the baseline a threshold is taken from, because the old baseline was shown unreproducible by the binary of the commit that produced it, on a box proven quiet, in an A/B rather than in a single run. The practical consequence of leaving it was a gate that printed WARN sprites.present.ms on every green run - a warning that always fires is a warning nobody reads.
